evals.query: My Kora 2.0 HTTP server is generated from an OpenAPI contract with an apiKey security scheme named apiKeyAuth. How do I validate the API key on every request?
expected_behavior: Declares HttpServerPrincipalExtractor<String, Principal> with TWO type arguments, from io.koraframework.http.server.common.auth
Binds it with @Tag(ApiSecurity.ApiKeyAuth.class) — the tag named after the security scheme, PascalCased
Declares it as a default method on @KoraApp or a @Module interface, or as a tagged @Component class, but not both
Returns null to reject, explaining that the generated interceptor then throws HttpServerResponseException.of(401, "Unauthorized")
Uses io.koraframework.common.Principal and a record/data class implementing it
Externalizes the expected key via @ConfigSource and ${ENV} substitution rather than inlining it
Does not emit CompletableFuture/CompletionStage, Mono, or suspend anywhere in the extractor
Does not tell the user to add the generated ApiSecurity to the @KoraApp interface list
Identifies the wrong tag as the cause: the global interceptor tag in Kora 2.0 is @Tag(HttpServer.class), io.koraframework.http.server.common.HttpServer

Explains that HttpServerModule still exists so the old tag compiles, but HttpServerModule#publicHttpApiRouter collects @Tag(HttpServer.class) All<HttpServerInterceptor>, so the interceptor is never invoked
Stresses the security impact: authentication silently disappears with no error, warning or log line
Does not change the intercept signature, which is already correct
Recommends a @KoraAppTest asserting 401 on an unauthenticated request, since a successful compile proves nothing here

evals.query: Porting a Kora 1.x service to 2.0. My extractor is tagged @Tag(ApiSecurity.SecurityRequirementTag1.class) and now the build fails with 'cannot find symbol: SecurityRequirementTag1'. What replaced it?
expected_behavior: States that ordinal SecurityRequirementTagN tags no longer exist in Kora 2.0
Explains the 2.0 rule: the tag is derived from the name in components.securitySchemes, sanitized to an identifier and PascalCased (apiKeyAuth -> ApiSecurity.ApiKeyAuth, oAuth -> ApiSecurity.OAuth)
Tells the user to open the generated ApiSecurity in build/generated and copy the tag and the extractor parameter type verbatim
Mentions that ANDed schemes produce an extractor tag joined with 'With' and an <Tag>AuthData record replacing String as the first type argument
Does not invent a tag name or guess without pointing at the generated file

evals.query: In Kora 1.x my interceptor stashed the user in Context (Context.current().set(USER_KEY, user)) and the controller read it back. In Kora 2.0 Context does not resolve. How do I hand the principal to my handler now?
expected_behavior: States that Context was removed from Kora 2.0 entirely — it is not merely absent from the HTTP APIs
Points to io.koraframework.common.Principal, which holds a ScopedValue<Principal>
Shows the interceptor publishing with Principal.with(principal, () -> chain.process(request))
Shows the handler reading with Principal.current(), noting it is @Nullable and needs a cast to the concrete principal type
Notes the binding lives only for the duration of chain.process and is not visible on an arbitrary executor the handler submits to
Does not propose a request-attribute bag, a ThreadLocal, or request.getAttribute(...)
Changes the type to HttpServerPrincipalExtractor<String, Principal> — two type parameters, credential type first
Removes CompletableFuture entirely: extract is synchronous and returns @Nullable P directly
Notes that the credential handed to a bearer extractor is the WHOLE Authorization header, so the code must strip the 'Bearer ' prefix itself
Returns null on a missing or invalid token instead of throwing SecurityException
Explains that an uncaught SecurityException becomes HTTP 500 with the exception message in the body, because SecurityException has no meaning anywhere in Kora 2.0
Does not introduce Mono, Flux, or a suspend function

Fixes all four problems: drops suspend, drops the Context parameter, changes the tag to @Tag(HttpServer::class), and replaces SecurityException with HttpServerResponseException.of(401, "Unauthorized")
Produces override fun intercept(request: HttpServerRequest, chain: HttpServerInterceptor.InterceptChain): HttpServerResponse
Calls chain.process(request) with the single argument
Flags the tag fix as the security-critical one — it compiles either way but authentication silently never runs with the old tag
If it publishes a principal, uses Principal.with with both type arguments explicit, e.g. Principal.with<HttpServerResponse, RuntimeException>(p) { chain.process(request) }

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 build fails with 'Multiple components match dependency HttpServerPrincipalExtractor<String, Principal> with tag ApiSecurity.ApiKeyAuth'. I have a @Component @Tag(ApiSecurity.ApiKeyAuth.class) ApiKeyExtractor class and also a default method with the same @Tag on my @KoraApp.
expected_behavior: Identifies the duplication: exactly one provider may exist per type-plus-tag, and both forms are registering the same one
Tells the user to delete one — either the tagged @Component class or the module default method
Notes the mirror-image failure, 'No component found for dependency', when neither is declared or when the generic arguments do not match the generated ApiSecurity parameter exactly
Explains separately that a @Mapping mapper class is instantiated inline only when it is final, has a public no-arg constructor and carries no @Tag, and otherwise must be a @Component
Does not suggest @DefaultComponent on the user's extractor as a way to paper over the conflict without saying which declaration is removed

evals.query: How do I enforce OAuth2 scopes on my OpenAPI-generated Kora 2.0 endpoints, and can I return 403 when a scope is missing?
expected_behavior: Declares HttpServerPrincipalExtractor<String, PrincipalWithScopes> — the second type argument becomes PrincipalWithScopes for oauth2/openIdConnect schemes
Uses io.koraframework.http.common.auth.PrincipalWithScopes and implements Collection<String> scopes()
Binds one extractor per scheme with @Tag(ApiSecurity.<SchemeName>.class), noting that per-scope interceptor tags like OAuth_PetsRead do not each need their own extractor

States that the generated interceptor checks scopes().contains(...) itself and answers 403 Forbidden when the extractor returned a principal but a required scope is missing, and 401 Unauthorized when no alternative authenticated
Keeps HttpServerResponseException.of(403, ...) from the delegate (after Principal.current()) only for rules the contract cannot express, such as roles or ownership
Does not invent a Kora @Scope, @Secured or @PreAuthorize annotation
anti_behavior: Claims the generated security interceptor never returns 403 and tells the user to re-implement the contract's scope check in every delegate

evals.query: My OpenAPI-generated Kora server returns a plaintext 401 'Unauthorized'. I need a JSON error body for auth failures. I already registered an interceptor through the generator's `interceptors` config option but it never sees the 401.
expected_behavior: Explains that the generated security interceptor is emitted first on the controller method and is therefore OUTERMOST among per-route interceptors, so an `interceptors`-option interceptor nests inside it and cannot observe the 401 it throws
Directs the user to a global interceptor annotated @Tag(HttpServer.class) — globals wrap the whole routed invocation, including the generated security interceptor
Shows catching HttpServerResponseException and re-rendering it via HttpServerResponse.of(e.code(), HttpBody.json(...))
Warns against catching bare Exception, which would convert genuine bugs into tidy JSON
May mention that several global interceptors are allowed, sorted by simple class name, with the alphabetically last one outermost
Does not claim only one global interceptor is permitted — that was the Kora 1.x rule

evals.query: I have a Kora 2.0 HTTP server with no OpenAPI contract. How do I require an X-API-Key header on all endpoints and make the caller identity available inside my controllers?
expected_behavior: Implements HttpServerInterceptor with the synchronous signature intercept(HttpServerRequest, InterceptChain) returning HttpServerResponse, importing it from io.koraframework.http.server.common.interceptor
Reads the header via request.headers().getFirst(...)
Rejects with HttpServerResponseException.of(401, ...) or an early HttpServerResponse.of(401, HttpBody.plaintext(...)), not with SecurityException
Publishes the caller with Principal.with(principal, () -> chain.process(request)) and reads it in the controller with Principal.current()
Registers it globally with @Component plus @Tag(HttpServer.class), or scopes it with @InterceptWith on the @HttpController class or @HttpRoute method
Does not use Context, request.getAttribute, or a ThreadLocal

evals.query: In my Kora 2.0 controller I want the x-user-id header as a typed Caller argument. My mapper needs an injected UserService and the build now says 'No component found for dependency CallerMapper'.
expected_behavior: Implements HttpServerRequestMapper<Caller> from io.koraframework.http.server.common.request and injects it with @Mapping(CallerMapper.class)
Diagnoses the error correctly: a @Mapping mapper is instantiated inline by the processor only when the class is final, has a single public no-arg constructor, and carries no @Tag
Since this mapper has a constructor dependency, it is injected from the graph and therefore needs @Component
Mentions the mirror-image failure — adding @Component to a final, no-arg, untagged mapper yields 'Multiple components match dependency'
Notes that a non-final Java mapper class is injected even with a no-arg constructor, unlike Kotlin where classes are final by default
Recommends an interceptor plus Principal.current() when the goal is authentication rather than plain request context

evals.query: Implement HTTP Basic authentication for my OpenAPI-generated Kora 2.0 server. In 1.x the extractor received the base64 blob directly — is that still true?
expected_behavior: Corrects the premise: for http basic/bearer and oauth2 schemes the generated interceptor passes request.headers().getFirst("Authorization") unchanged, so the value includes the 'Basic ' prefix
Strips the prefix before base64-decoding and splits username:password with a limit of 2
Binds HttpServerPrincipalExtractor<String, Principal> with @Tag(ApiSecurity.BasicAuth.class)
Returns null on a missing header, a malformed base64 payload, or failed credential validation instead of throwing
Recommends serving Basic auth over HTTPS because the credential is encoded, not encrypted
Contrasts with apiKey schemes, where the value is the raw header/query/cookie value with no prefix
Identifies nullability as the cause even though the error message never mentions it
Explains that http-server-common is @NullMarked and the contract is @Nullable P extract(HttpServerRequest, @Nullable T token)
Fixes the signature to override fun extract(request: HttpServerRequest, token: String?): Principal?
Handles the null token by returning null rather than throwing
Does not suggest annotating the Kotlin declaration with JSpecify @Nullable, which is not how Kotlin expresses nullability

evals.query: What type should my principal class be in a Kora 2.0 HTTP server, where does Principal come from, and how does a handler get hold of it?
expected_behavior: States that Principal is io.koraframework.common.Principal, a framework interface, and the principal is a record/data class implementing it
Uses io.koraframework.http.common.auth.PrincipalWithScopes when oauth2 scopes are involved
States that Principal.current() DOES exist in Kora 2.0, backed by ScopedValue<Principal>, and is published by Principal.with(...)
Notes that Principal.current() is @Nullable and returns null on anonymous routes, so the result needs a null check and a cast
Explains that the declared type argument in HttpServerPrincipalExtractor stays Principal (or PrincipalWithScopes) even though the extractor returns the concrete type
Does not equate Principal with java.security.Principal or a third-party user-details type, and does not claim there is no current-principal accessor
